ai.description: The Mudur Caecilian reaches 20–25 cm in length. It is dark purplish-brown with a pale snout and vent. It is distinguished by its 115–120 primary annuli and lack of secondary grooves.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis madhavai* is best distinguished by its unique lack of secondary annuli, meaning its body segments are not subdivided, unlike most other Indian caecilians.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis madhavai* inhabits moist, shaded soil within tropical evergreen forests and cardamom plantations in the Western Ghats at altitudes between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mudur caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis madhavai* is oviparous, laying clutches of 10–18 eggs in underground nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis madhavai* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it is found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Mudur Caecilian produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of clicks or chirps, typically heard from underground burrows in moist, leaf-littered soil.
